articles.title: AFL sanctions Lachie Cowan after Carlton player’s illicit drug use at house party
articles.summary: Blues defender apologises after ‘conduct unbecoming’ verdict. Handed two-match ban and fined following off-season night out. Carlton defender Lachie Cowan has received a “wake-up call” after being suspended for two matches for the use of an illicit substance during a night out last weekend.
body: In addition to the ban, which will be served at the beginning of next season, Cowan was handed a $5,000 suspended fine along with a “notifiable adverse finding” under the AFL’s illicit drugs policy.
He must also undertake further education on illicit substances and their effects.
A club statement on Sunday afternoon said Cowan had “received medical treatment and underwent observation, before being discharged a short time later”.
Blues teammate Will Hayward was also admitted to hospital and required stitches to a minor cut to his head in what Carlton said were “separate circumstances”.

articles.title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez goals seal Bournemouth’s historic home win in Europe
articles.summary: An impossible dream realised: the Vitality Stadium staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. No wins yet in the Premier League, but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose.
body: Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.”

Bournemouth’s new head coach has described the chaos of English football, midfield areas that can resemble a rolling maul, but he has pledged to learn and adapt. “I believe in this team and know they are always confident despite a difficult situation,” Rose said. “If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans then we are hard to play and it’s hard to beat us. That’s what we should take into the next game.”

articles.title: Minus 17 to European dreams as Bournemouth fairytale continues
articles.summary: It was a night 127 years in the making as Bournemouth added another chapter to their fairytale with victory in their first-ever European home game.
body: And it was no coincidence that was the song chosen at the Vitality Stadium before Bournemouth's first European home game in the club's 127-year history.

As supporters lucky enough to bag a ticket for the historic occasion waved flags to the Andy Williams classic, a giant tifo rose from behind one of the stands, bearing the words 'Minus 17 to European dreams. AFC Bournemouth, established 1899'.
As recently as 2008, a night like this would have been unthinkable for Cherries supporters.
Just 18 years ago, Bournemouth were facing the prospect of no longer existing.

articles.summary: Halpin’s first playoff homer puts Cleveland ahead. Williams strikes out nine as Guardians win 3-2. Cleveland bullpen retires 11 of final 12 Rays batters. Petey Halpin hit a go-ahead two-run homer, Gavin Williams struck out nine over five innings and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Tampa Bay Rays…
body: Game 4 of the best-of-seven series is scheduled for Friday, though rain is forecast.

José Ramírez had two hits and Nathaniel Lowe added an RBI for the Guardians, who have won five of their last six playoff games since falling 2-0 behind the Chicago White Sox in their AL Division Series.

Williams allowed two runs over five innings while walking one. He is 2-0 with a 2.16 ERA and 33 strikeouts over 16 and two-thirds innings innings in four postseason appearances this year, including three starts.
Cleveland retired 16 of the Rays’ final 17 batters. Daniel Espino, Erik Sabrowski, Hunter Gaddis and Cade Smith combined to allow just one baserunner over the final four innings.

articles.title: Europa League: Lyon take down Crystal Palace as Benfica overwhelm Celtic
articles.summary: Sage loses 3-2 to former side; Benfica 4-1 Celtic. Juventus go top with 2-1 win over Celta Vigo. Pierre Sage endured a frustrating return to Lyon in the Europa League as his Crystal Palace side lost 3-2 to his former employers at the Groupama Stadium.
body: Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half without a shot on target for the visitors. Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break before Pavel Sulc restored the Ligue 1 side’s two-goal advantage. The Palace substitute Daichi Kamada pulled one back with nine minutes remaining in a better second half for Palace, who could not find an equaliser.

Days after beating his predecessor, the Nottingham Forest manager, Oliver Glasner, at Selhurst Park in the Premier League on Sunday, Sage found himself returning to the home of the club he managed for 14 months.
Ismaïla Sarr, who claimed the Conference League golden boot last season, was in the Crystal Palace starting lineup for the first time this season.

Celtic found a clinical Benfica side too much to handle during a 4-1 defeat in Lisbon. The Colombia striker Jhon Durán scored for the hosts with a penalty after just five minutes having been fouled by Dane Murray and completed his double in the 35th minute, after the defender Alexander Bah had doubled Benfica’s lead earlier in the half.

body: “I’m not as high on Miami as a lot of people are,” Van Gundy said in a podcast guesting. “They did go out and add some shooting around those guys, but the shooting that they added compromises them badly at the defensive end of the floor.”

Miami acquired Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis from the Milwaukee Bucks in late June, sending Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel’el Ware and Kasparas Jakucionis the other way. The Heat later signed Tim Hardaway Jr. and Klay Thompson to add perimeter shooting.

body: Dowdle was a full participant in practice for the first time in a while, offering encouraging news for a Pittsburgh offense that could use another reliable running back. The veteran has been sidelined with a toe injury, but his recent progress puts him in position to potentially return in Week 7.

Dowdle joined the Steelers after an impressive 2025 season with the Carolina Panthers, where he showed he could be a productive running back when given a meaningful workload. Fantasy football managers who relied on him last season know what he can bring to an offense, and Pittsburgh was hoping he could provide similar production after signing with the team.

However, Dowdle’s injury has given Jaylen Warren an opportunity to take control of the backfield, and he has made the most of it. Warren has been red-hot recently, delivering consistent production and establishing himself as one of Pittsburgh’s most important offensive weapons. His recent performances have made it difficult to imagine the Steelers significantly reducing his workload, even when Dowdle returns.

articles.title: Rutter scores twice as Brighton win big and go top in Conference League
articles.summary: Georginio Rutter scored twice and set up one as Brighton thrashed Kauno Zalgris 4-0 to get their Conference League campaign off to a winning start.
body: Brighton were dominant from the first whistle to the last against the Lithuanian Cup winners and took the lead through Rutter, but only after a VAR check. The ball had initially been deemed to have gone out of play before Ibrahim Osman's cut-back to the Frenchman, but the goal was awarded after review.

Rutter then turned provider as Brighton doubled their lead on the stroke of half-time when Hinshelwood - returning to the side for the first time since the Premier League opening weekend - slotted into the corner.
The third came after a lung-bursting run from Malick Yalcouye, who played Osman through to cross for Rutter to turn into the net with ease.

Matt O'Riley made it four with a header as he scored his first Brighton goal since August 2025. The Australia international should have got his second with another header late on, but was denied by an excellent save from Tomas Svedkauskas.

articles.title: LIV Golf accuses DP World Tour of interference in bankruptcy process
articles.summary: LIV Golf has accused the DP World Tour of interference in its bankruptcy proceedings at a hearing in which Bryson DeChambeau and others were released from their contracts.
body: The breakaway league is attempting to relaunch next year with new money from BC Partners Capital after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support having ploughed in $5bn (£3.7bn) over four years.
But in order to do that it has had to apply for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and, as a result, it has had to cancel the contracts of the existing players so they can be re-signed on new terms to LIV 2.0.

However, the DP World Tour confirmed this week it was taking a harder line than previously and any player committing to LIV 2.0 would be ineligible for its membership and therefore also ruled out of Ryder Cup contention.

It has been seen in many quarters as an attempt to deliver the final blow to LIV's fading hopes of survival and, according to reports in the US media, its attorney Robert Fitzgerald told the US Bankruptcy Court in New York: "We're continuing to monitor this situation very closely and we're quite concerned by it frankly.

articles.title: Does Anyone Actually Want To Win NFC (L)East? Predicting NFL's New Worst Division
articles.summary: The race to win the once-strong NFC East is looking like a war of attrition among four flawed and injured teams. Can anybody rise to the top of the pile?
body: The NFC East is as wide open as it’s been in years, for any team that wants to take it. It’s just not clear that any of them actually can.

Right now, this entire division is a jumbled, ugly mess. Just last weekend, the first-place New York Giants (yes, you read that right) literally fumbled away a shot to open a big lead in the division race. And they were only partially bailed out by the Washington Commanders’ mind-boggling inability to read the clock.

Meanwhile, in Philadelphia, the Eagles have half their roster on the injury report, including quarterback Jalen Hurts. A day after Hurts appeared on the injury report for the first time, it was announced that the quarterback would miss their Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers due to blood clots. And they just blew back-to-back games, including one where Nick Sirianni’s game management skills rivaled those of Dan Quinn. Yet, they’re still in better shape than the Dallas Cowboys, who are playing with the worst defense Jerry Jones’ "old man" money can buy.
